snippet.description:

Segundo uma atualização, o teto de uma loja de roupas e tecidos foi responsável pelo desabamento. Ainda de acordo com a Defesa Civil, informações preliminares indicam que cerca de 20 pessoas estão retidas em um cômodo cuja laje não foi atingida pelo desabamento. #CNNBrasil #nacional

During the defense case, Naresh Bhatt took the stand! Now, let's see the CROSS-EXAMINATION of this defendant. 

Case background: In July 2024, 28-year-old nurse and mother Mamta Kafle Bhatt vanished from her home in Manassas Park, Virginia. She was last seen on a video call with her mother on July 29. Her husband, Naresh Bhatt, later told police she had left for Texas or New York and cut off contact. Her body has never been found.
Coworkers asked for a welfare check on August 2 after she missed work. Naresh reported her missing on August 5. He was arrested on August 22, 2024, and a grand jury later indicted him on first-degree murder, concealment of a dead body, and physical defilement of a dead body. Prosecutors allege he killed Mamta in their home on or about July 30, 2024, dismembered her, and disposed of her remains in trash bags left at dumpsters and compactors around Manassas Park and Fairfax County. He has pleaded not guilty.
This is a no-body case. The Commonwealth says blood in the bedroom, closet, shower, and bathtub, Mamta’s DNA on a power saw, heavy water use, cleaning-product purchases, surveillance of bags being dumped, and internet searches about a spouse disappearing or dying will prove she was murdered and that Naresh did it. Prosecutors have also described a marriage already breaking down, including claims that Mamta was preparing to leave. The defense says there is a hole in that evidence the state cannot fill, and that marital problems are not proof of murder.
Jury selection began October 5, 2026, in Prince William County Circuit Court before Judge Kimberly Irving. Opening statements were October 7. Matthew Sweet opened for the Commonwealth. Chief Public Defender Tracey Lenox opened for the defense. The trial is expected to last about seven weeks.
Naresh Bhatt is presumed innocent unless and until a jury finds him guilty.

snippet.description:
Accédez à https://ground.news/ate : 40 % de réduction pour explorer l’outil qui décrypte le flux médiatique et analyse les infos à tous les niveaux.

Un Airbus A320 escorté par des avions de chasse français, un atterrissage sur la base militaire d'Évreux et une vague d'alertes à la bombe qui frappe l'Europe. Que s'est-il réellement passé ? Et pourquoi une fausse alerte peut-elle avoir des conséquences dramatiques ?

Le 5 novembre 2026, le vol Aer Lingus EI402 reliant Dublin à Rome est dérouté vers la base aérienne 105 d'Évreux après une alerte à la bombe. À bord : 151 passagers et 6 membres d'équipage.

Pendant ce temps, de nombreux autres vols sont visés en Europe. Des chasseurs sont mobilisés, des appareils déroutés et des équipes spécialisées interviennent.

Heureusement, aucun explosif n'est découvert dans les appareils inspectés.

Mais attention : une fausse alerte à la bombe n'est pas sans danger.

En 1977, une alerte à la bombe provoquait notamment la fermeture de l'aéroport de Grande Canarie et le déroutement d'avions vers Tenerife. L'enchaînement des événements allait contribuer à la catastrophe aérienne la plus meurtrière de l'histoire : 583 victimes.
